title: Container Logs and Output
subtopics: Understanding standard output and standard error
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of container logs and output.
Choose and interpret a suitable Docker example connected to container logs and output.
Predict an expected result and verify it using observable evidence in a controlled environment.

content.intro: This lesson covers Container Logs and Output. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Treat container logs and output as a behavior to explain and verify, not a command to memorize. Identify the Docker component or setting involved, predict the outcome, then confirm it using a small isolated lab and a recorded result. Learning container logs and output helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

items.title: Reading logs
items.text: Logs are most useful when they include enough context to correlate a failure without leaking credentials or personal data. Check retention and rotation as well as message content.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with the supplied example for container logs and output. Before running it, state what you expect to happen. Compare the real output with that prediction, then change one variable or setting in a disposable lab to test the boundary of the idea. If a command is not supported on your operating system or installed Docker version, consult the linked official reference and record the actual version rather than guessing.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Container Logs and Output
content_blocks.code:
docker ps -a
docker logs --tail 50 CONTAINER_NAME
docker inspect CONTAINER_NAME
content_blocks.expected_output: The commands show container state, recent application output, and the inspectable runtime configuration for a chosen container.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Replace CONTAINER_NAME with a container from your disposable lab. Preserve the exact error text before changing settings.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Read-only diagnostics; no reset is required.
content_blocks.safety_note: Do not include secrets or personal data in captured logs or incident reports.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Keep this lesson in draft while reviewing: Container Logs and Output. Capture the command/configuration, expected and actual result, one failure or edge case, and cleanup performed. This course does not award XP from content files; CodeLeaf backend rules remain authoritative.

task: Apply container logs and output to a small local case. Record the configuration or command, expected result, observed result, one limitation/edge case, and how you verified the result.
hints: Begin with read-only inspection commands and identify the active Docker context before any mutating action.
Use a disposable name, local test image, and synthetic data; change one thing at a time.
If the outcome differs, preserve the exact error and logs, check the official reference for your installed version, and document the verified fix.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
